category_title: Low-proficiency students who experience high anxiety and lack of confidence due to linguistic barriers
minimal_context: The student is writing a 300-word journal reflection on Blackboard about their linguistic challenges during their first year at the university.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please log into Blackboard and write your 300-word journal reflection about the language challenges you have faced during your first year at the university.

STUDENT: This is my first year come to United States, so my English is not very good. I cannot remember many words and I do not know how to write so much words.

TUTOR: Just write what you can for now.

STUDENT: When I write my essay, I meet many problems. My grammar is not very good. I look up the words in the dictionary, ask my roommate about my grammar.

TUTOR: Keep working on it and submit what you have.

STUDENT: I felt not good, I tried my best to write it but it was so bad. Although I was so unhappy, I knew it was my problem. I came back home to rewrite my essay.

options.A: Implement a sequenced writing project where the student writes four journal reflections on the same subject over the course of the semester.
options.B: Secure and participate in family counseling through the Department of Human Services to address the student's challenges over the course of the semester.
options.C: Engage in shared discourse and provide direct instruction in coping strategies within the online Blackboard routine over the course of the semester.
options.D: View the student as a gifted underachiever struggling with the reflection for a specific reason, viewing their underachievement as a promise for potential.
